'''Norman Rostoker''' (August 16, 1925 – December 25, 2014) was a Canadian [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physicist]] known for being a pioneer in developing clean [[Fusion power|plasma-based fusion]] energy.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ps.uci.edu/memorial/Rostoker|title=Norman Rostoker {{!}} Physical Sciences Memorial|website=ps.uci.edu|access-date=2020-02-16|archive-date=February 16, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200216234524/https://ps.uci.edu/memorial/Rostoker|url-status=dead}}</ref> He co-founded [[TAE Technologies]] (formerly known as Tri Alpha Energy) in 1998 and held 27 U.S. Patents on [[Plasma acceleration|plasma-based fusion accelerators]].

The [[Korringa–Kohn–Rostoker method]], a theory in [[solid-state physics]], is named after him.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kohn|first1=W.|last2=Rostoker|first2=N.|date=1954|title=Solution of the Schrödinger Equation in Periodic Lattices with an Application to Metallic Lithium|journal=Physical Review|language=en|volume=94|issue=5|pages=1111–1120|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.94.1111|bibcode=1954PhRv...94.1111K |issn=0031-899X}}</ref><ref> [[David Clary| Clary, David C.]] (2024). [https://doi.org/10.1142/13806 Walter Kohn: From Kindertransport and Internment to DFT and the Nobel Prize]. World Scientific Publishing. </ref>

== Early life and career ==
Rostoker studied at the [[University of Toronto]], where he received his master's degree in physics in 1947, and received his doctorate in 1950 at the [[Carnegie Institute of Technology]], where he did research from 1948. From 1953 to 1956, he was at the [[Armour Research Foundation|Armor Research Foundation]] and from 1956 to 1967 at [[General Atomics]] in San Diego, from 1965 as manager for fusion and plasma physics projects. He was also a professor at the [[University of California, San Diego]] from 1962 to 1965. From 1967, he was an IBM Professor of Engineering at [[Cornell University]], where he headed the Faculty of Applied Physics from 1967 to 1970. There, he was one of the founders of the laboratory for pulsed electron and ion beams. From 1973, he was professor of physics at the [[University of California, Irvine]], where he headed the faculty of physics from 1973 to 1976. He was Professor Emeritus there since 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11608041.html|title=Rostoker, Norman|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-02-23}}</ref>

== Scientific contributions ==
Initially, Rostoker dealt with [[explosive]]s and [[shaped charge]]s, [[band theory]] and [[nuclear reactor]]s, but turned to [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]] around 1958. His research included the physics of high intensity [[ion beam]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Robertson|first1=S.|last2=Ishizuka|first2=H.|last3=Peter|first3=W.|last4=Rostoker|first4=N.|date=1981|title=Propagation of an Intense Ion Beam Transverse to a Magnetic Field|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=47|issue=7|pages=508–511|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.47.508|bibcode=1981PhRvL..47..508R }}</ref> nonlinear plasma properties,<ref name="escholarship.org">{{Cite journal|last1=Nebenzahl|first1=I.|last2=Ron|first2=Amiram|last3=Rostoker|first3=Norman|date=1988|title=Reflected phase-conjugate wave in a plasma|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=60|issue=11|pages=1030–1032|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.60.1030|pmid=10037923|bibcode=1988PhRvL..60.1030N |s2cid=34688572 |url=http://www.escholarship.org/uc/item/0gh7072t|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and high density [[Pinch (plasma physics)|pinch plasma]] confinement devices.<ref name="escholarship.org"/>

Rostoker pursued alternative concepts for civil nuclear fusion using particle accelerator technologies and the concepts of [[magnetized target fusion]]. In 1998, he was instrumental in founding the then [[Tri-Alpha Energy|Tri Alpha Energy]] in the Los Angeles area,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/exclusive-secretive-fusion-company-claims-reactor-breakthrough|title=Exclusive: Secretive fusion company claims reactor breakthrough|last1=Clery|first1=Daniel|date=2015-08-24|website=Science {{!}} AAAS|language=en|access-date=2020-02-23}}</ref> which was pursuing the project of a [[Colliding Beam Fusion Reactor|colliding beam fusion reactor]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Rostoker|first=N.|date=1997|title=Colliding Beam Fusion Reactor|journal=Science|volume=278|issue=5342|pages=1419–1422|doi=10.1126/science.278.5342.1419|pmid=9367946|bibcode=1997Sci...278.1419R |issn=0036-8075}}</ref> [[Proton beam|Beams of protons]] and boron are converted into a plasma state that is held together by [[magnetic field]]s that are generated by the flow of particles in a cylindrical plasma itself, which is also known as a [[field-reversed configuration]] (FRC). Two such plasmas are then collided at high speed and form a cigar-shaped configuration that is up to 3 m long and 40&nbsp;cm wide. The use of boron and protons in the fusion plasma does not generate high-energy neutrons like the [[tokamak]]. According to Rostoker, neutral particles are then injected tangentially at high speed onto the plasma cloud, which follow orbits at the edge of the plasma and serve as a kind of protection against the cooling of the plasma by escaping particles.<ref name=":1" />

In 2015, Tri Alpha announced the successful maintenance of an FRC plasma over five milliseconds.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gota|first1=H.|last2=Binderbauer|first2=M.W.|last3=Tajima|first3=T.|last4=Putvinski|first4=S.|last5=Tuszewski|first5=M.|last6=Dettrick|first6=S.|last7=Garate|first7=E.|last8=Korepanov|first8=S.|last9=Smirnov|first9=A.|last10=Thompson|first10=M.C.|last11=Trask|first11=E.|date=2017|title=Achievement of field-reversed configuration plasma sustainment via 10 MW neutral-beam injection on the C-2U device|journal=Nuclear Fusion|volume=57|issue=11|pages=116021|doi=10.1088/1741-4326/aa7d7b|bibcode=2017NucFu..57k6021G |s2cid=19931583 |issn=0029-5515}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 1962, Rostoker was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1962&unit_id=APS&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|last=|first=|date=|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2020-02-16}}{{dead link|date=May 2020|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> and then subsequently awarded the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] in 1988.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Rostoker&first_nm=Norman&year=1988|title=1988 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|last=|first=|date=|website=American Physical Society|language=en|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110516053018/http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Rostoker&first_nm=Norman&year=1988|archive-date=2011-05-16|access-date=2020-02-16}}</ref>

Rostoker was also awarded the UCI Medal by the [[University of California, Irvine]] and was inducted into the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":0" />
